None contains sufficiently distinctive shared language or parallel legal or administrative machinery to establish a material drafting template.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"There is, however, one objection made by opponents of H.R. 331 and H.R. 49 which I believe requires further discussion because it goes beyond the question of statehood and raises a fundamental constitutional issue.","parent_excerpt":"The people of the District of Columbia should not be placed in a different status from that of the people of all other American cities and almost all democratic capitals of the world in so far as local self-government is concerned.","explanation":"C18 shares a constitutional self-government theme, but not the child's specific objection-and-rebuttal language or machinery."},{"child_excerpt":"This was one of the great compromises which the Federalist says was a result \"not of theory, but of a spirit of amity...\"","parent_excerpt":"Writing on this subject in The Federalist, James Madison said that the inhabitants of the District \"will have . . . their choice in the election of the government which is to exercise authority over them\"","explanation":"Both cite The Federalist in support of democratic representation, but the quotations and constitutional propositions are different; the shared source alone is insufficient."},{"child_excerpt":"This argument is not only entirely without merit, but also directly attacks a basic tenet of the constitutional system","parent_excerpt":"The resolution you have transmitted to me proceeds, however, by a process of reasoning which I do not follow","explanation":"C02 similarly pivots from support for legislation to rebutting an opposing argument, but this is a generic persuasive-letter structure rather than concrete shared drafting."}]}
